1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 c5 3.e3 g6 4.Nc3 Bg7 5.Nf3.strategy: The natural developing move: the knight adds a defender to d4, which Black's c-pawn is pressing, and covers e5. White builds a compact, solid set-up and leaves it to Black whether to exchange on d4 or keep the tension.

Castles early, tucking the king behind the fianchettoed bishop and connecting the rooks. With the kingside settled, Black decides when to challenge d4 with the c-pawn, and White has not yet claimed more space than Black can contest.
